name: Minecraft: Nukkit
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Nukkit, CloudburstMC's Minecraft: Bedrock Edition server written in Java, with its own plugins. Installs any Nukkit build, checked against the repository's checksums.
startup: mkdir -p plugins/bStats; b=plugins/bStats/config.yml; touch $b; if ! grep -q "^serverUuid:" $b; then read -r u < /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid; echo "serverUuid: \"$u\"" >> $b; fi; grep -q "^logFailedRequests:" $b || echo "logFailedRequests: false" >> $b; if grep -q "^enabled:" $b; then sed -i "s/^enabled:.*/enabled: {{BSTATS}}/" $b; else echo "enabled: {{BSTATS}}" >> $b; fi; read -r need 2>/dev/null < .raptor-java || need=8; java -version 2>&1 | awk -F'"' -v need="$need" '/version/ { split($2, v, "."); have = (v[1] == "1") ? v[2] : v[1]; if (have + 0 < need + 0) { printf "This server needs Java %s or newer, but Java %s is chosen. Choose Java %s or newer in Startup, then start the server again.\n", need, have, need; exit 1 } exit }' && exec java -Xms128M -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=85.0 -XX:+IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -XX:+DisableExplicitGC -XX:+PerfDisableSharedMem -jar {{SERVER_JARFILE}} --language eng

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Minecraft: Nukkit. Downloads a Nukkit build from CloudburstMC's Maven
# repository and checks it against the repository's checksum. Worlds,
# plugins and settings are never touched, and the jar is only replaced once
# the new one has downloaded and checked out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=https://repo.opencollab.dev/maven-snapshots/cn/nukkit/nukkit/1.0-SNAPSHOT
jar="${SERVER_JARFILE:-server.jar}"
get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 "$1"; }
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# The Java version the jar was built for, from its main class's file format.
jar_java() {
    local main major
    main=$(unzip -p "$1" META-INF/MANIFEST.MF | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^Main-Class: *//p' | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$main" ] || { echo 8; return; }
    major=$(unzip -p "$1" "${main//.//}.class" | od -An -j6 -N2 -tu1 | awk '{ print $1 * 256 + $2 }')
    if [ -n "$major" ] && [ "$major" -gt 52 ]; then echo $((major - 44)); else echo 8; fi
}

# Every build, oldest first: 1.0-<date>.<time>-<build number>.
builds=$(get "https://repo.opencollab.dev/api/maven/details/maven-snapshots/cn/nukkit/nukkit/1.0-SNAPSHOT" |
    jq -r '.files[].name' | sed -nE 's/^nukkit-(1\.0-[0-9]{8}\.[0-9]{6}-([0-9]+))\.jar$/\2 \1/p' | sort -n) ||
    fail "CloudburstMC's repository can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
[ -n "$builds" ] || fail "CloudburstMC's repository lists no Nukkit builds right now. Reinstall to try again later."
want="${NUKKIT_VERSION:-latest}"
case "$want" in
latest | "") version=$(tail -n 1 <<<"$builds" | cut -d' ' -f2) ;;
*) version=$(awk -v w="$want" '$1 == w || $2 == w { print $2 }' <<<"$builds") ;;
esac
[ -n "$version" ] ||
    fail "Nukkit has no build $want. Set Version to latest, or to a build number such as $(tail -n 1 <<<"$builds" | cut -d' ' -f1)."
build=${version##*-}

sum=$(get "$repo/nukkit-$version.jar.sha256" | cut -c1-64) || fail "CloudburstMC's repository can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
if [ -f "$jar" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$jar" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "Nukkit build $build is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Nukkit build $build"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$jar.new" "$repo/nukkit-$version.jar"
    [ "$(sha256sum "$jar.new" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] || { rm -f "$jar.new"; fail "The download didn't match the repository's checksum. Reinstall to try again."; }
    mv -f "$jar.new" "$jar"
fi
java=$(jar_java "$jar")
echo "$java" > .raptor-java
echo "Installed Nukkit build $build. It needs Java $java or newer."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Nukkit build, such as 1253, or latest for the newest one. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Jar file
variables.description: The name of the server's jar file.

variables.name: Usage statistics
variables.description: Send anonymous statistics about the server and its plugins to bStats.org, where plugin authors see them (true or false).
